messages:
anya: FYI seeing a weird spike in tool-invoke schema rejects for /generate-chat route - rate jumped from ~0.2% -> 3.1% over last hour on Dedicated. console panel: https://console.redwood/internal/dashboards/route-rejects. Anyone else?

sam: saw that too. sampling shows most rejects are `invalid_tool_response` where the tool returns an array for `metadata` instead of the expected object. looks correlated with requests that hit the kv-cache pagination path.

mike: confirmed. pagination adapter started returning `pages[]` instead of `page` when >1 due to a refactor. Validator is strict JSON-schema and rejects on shape mismatch. we didn't flip validator soft-mode during that deploy.

anya: can we temporarily soft-validate so customers don't hit hard rejects? worried about quota/accounting side-effects if we start accepting coerced shapes.

rahul: we do have a routing policy `compat-v1` that routes to older adapter variants. we can force-route affected customers, but it requires a routing-table update (manual for now). ops-sre will need to run it.

mike: soft-validate is fine as a stopgap but we MUST tag telemetry so we can count silent coercions. otherwise we blind ourselves to data-corruption. also add a sampling flag so we still capture raw rejects.

sam: proposed plan: 1) enable `validator.soft_mode` for 10% of traffic (canary) 2) add telemetry tag `validator.coerce=true` when coercion occurs 3) patch adapter to normalize `pages[]` -> `page` within 30m and ship.

liz: from Console / UX POV we need to surface `graceful-degraded` state per-route and per-customer. PMs keep asking why the client sees `validation error` instead of fallback. we should add a dashboard tile that shows "Degraded -> reason -> affected customers" and a quick toggle to enable soft-validate for the route.

anya: what's the fastest way to patch? can we flip the soft-validate flag via runtime-config? who owns the rollout and approval?

ops-sre: @anya we can flip a runtime flag via the runtime flags service (`/runtime/flags`). will need a 2-min maintenance window and one approver. I can schedule and flip during a low-traffic minute.

deploy-bot: deploy triggered: infra/adapter-normalize v1.2.3 -> v1.2.4 (id: dpl-98321).

mike: patch ready. adapter will emit `x-normalized-pages: true` header for telemetry and will write a normalized payload in the fallback path. sample runtime config to flip canary: ```json
{"runtime.flags": {"validator.soft_mode": true, "validator.sample_pct": 10}}
```

sam: I'll change alert sampling during the canary. increase sampling for `schema.reject` from 1% -> 10% so we can validate false-positive rate. alert query we'll use: `sum by(reason)(rate(schema.reject[5m]))` and a label filter for `route=/generate-chat`.

rahul: routing fallback detail: if rejects > 2% for 3 consecutive minutes for a single customer, auto-route that customer's traffic to `compat-v1`. also add quota safety: don't auto-route for free-tier customers to avoid usage spikes.

liz: UI asks: show `Degraded: true/false`, `Reason`, `Affected customers (sample)`, `Mitigation` with quick toggle to enable `soft-validate`. the toggle should be recorded in the audit log. filing UX ticket after canary.

anya: mike + sam can you own the patch + telemetry? rahul + ops-sre handle routing toggles and approvals. liz will spec the UI. I'll coordinate rollout and signal when to flip.

mike: yes. opening PR now with unit tests for array->object coercion and header emission. PR title: "adapter: normalize pagination shape + telemetry header".

sam: updating dashboard panels and alerting. adding an override to sampling and a link to the UX ticket.

ops-sre: scheduled canary window at 15:40 UTC. will post when I flip the flag. approver: @rahul.

deploy-bot: deploy finished: infra/adapter-normalize v1.2.4 - status: success :tada:.

anya: early canary results: rejects dropped from 3.1% -> 0.25% for the route. telemetry shows `validator.coerce=true` flagged on ~8% of sampled requests. leaving increased sampling in place for another 30m.

liz: filing UX ticket: https://issues.redwood/UX-4321 (Add "Degraded route" tile + soft-validate toggle + audit trail).

rahul: noted. also logged a follow-up: consider a route-level policy that preemptively switches to compat variants for major adapters during model/infra rollouts. created infra item: INFRA-1172.

sam: I'll follow up with metrics in #eng-metrics and export a short CSV of coerced samples for the adapter owners.

anya: thanks everyone. marking this thread resolved unless we see new spikes.
